I fitted models to the 300 measured steels, checked them with five-fold cross-validation, and compared predictions against similar-composition heat-treatment examples.

| Candidate | Predicted Yield Strength (MPa) | Predicted Toughness (J) | Role |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **c010** | ~290 | ~360 | High-toughness endpoint |
| **c007** | ~400 | ~200 | Additional toughness-side coverage |
| **c085** | ~730 | ~195 | Balanced strength–toughness point |
| **c049** | ~1,160 | ~115 | Higher-strength intermediate point |
| **c041** | ~1,330 | ~70 | High-strength endpoint |

The training evidence particularly supports **c085**, whose nearby same-composition treatment achieved **710 MPa / 230 J**, and **c041**, whose tempering temperature lies between measured treatments achieving **1,340 MPa / 61 J** and **1,090 MPa / 88 J**.

These are predictions, not measurements. Toughness is substantially less predictable than strength, and **c049** has additional uncertainty because its unaged condition lacks a direct training match. Uncertainty-sensitive hypervolume comparisons favored **c007** for the fifth slot over adding the closely related **c072** alongside c041.

Final: c010, c007, c085, c049, c041
